 NBA Predictions and Moneyline Picks Today: Friday, Nov. 20
 Jon Metler 
 • Betting Analyst 
 5+ years betting experience 
 Updated: 
Nov 20, 2026 , 03:39 PM ET
 • 4 min read 
 The Nuggets host the Rockets in NBA Cup action, and betting analyst Jon Metler is backing Denver in his latest NBA moneyline picks.
 Jump to section: 
 Moneyline Picks 
 Analysis 
 ML Combo 
 More coverage 
 Photo By - Reuters Connect. NBA Moneyline Picks, Devin Booker, Nikola Jokic and Scottie Barnes 
 A nine-game NBA Cup slate tips off tonight, Friday, Nov. 20, with the Charlotte Hornets visiting the Atlanta Hawks at 7 p.m. ET. It wraps up at 10 p.m. ET with the Sacramento Kings at the Los Angeles Lakers and the Houston Rockets at the Denver Nuggets.
 Our NBA moneyline picks cover every matchup in tipoff order, with probabilities based on prediction market prices. The Lakers are the biggest favorites at 88%, while the Toronto Raptors are the steepest underdogs we're backing at 29%.
 Find more analysis and predictions on our NBA picks page, or check our NBA against the spread predictions for tonight's slate.

 Hornets vs Hawks: Hawks
 Trade 70% at Polymarket  → 
 Brandon Miller's return gives the Charlotte Hornets another reliable offensive option and takes some of the scoring burden off Coby White.
 However, the Atlanta Hawks have the point-of-attack and wing defenders to disrupt the actions Charlotte wants to run through Miller and White.
 At 70%, I still see a small edge on the Hawks at this price.
 For more on this matchup, see our Hornets vs. Hawks prediction .
 Raptors vs Pistons: Raptors
 Trade 29% at Polymarket → 
 I price the Toronto Raptors closer to 34%, so I'm hitting the button at 29%.
 Cade Cunningham sat out Wednesday for the Detroit Pistons , while Scottie Barnes was also sidelined for Toronto. I expect both players to return for this matchup, and they're included in my projections.
 With both teams playing the second night of a back-to-back, I view those absences as load management rather than injury concerns.
 RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles have also been ruled out for Toronto, but both absences are already accounted for in my projections and reflected in the updated market price.
 Get the full matchup breakdown in our Raptors vs. Pistons prediction .
 Magic vs Nets: Magic
 Trade 68% at Polymarket  → 
 Who do the Brooklyn Nets have that can slow down Franz Wagner at the point of attack?
 The Nets lack a defender with the size and speed to match up with Wagner. That is a significant problem, since he's the primary engine of the Orlando Magic's offense with Paolo Banchero sidelined by injury.
 At 66%, the edge on the Magic isn't massive, but there's enough value at this price for me to hit the button.
 Pacers vs Cavaliers: Cavaliers
 Trade 68% at Polymarket  → 
 I'm seeing a small edge on the Cleveland Cavaliers , but that's with Indiana Pacers guard Andrew Nembhard projected to play 31 minutes, which is far from a guarantee.
 Nembhard has now missed consecutive games, suggesting this is a legitimate injury concern rather than routine load management.
 I'd still back the Cavaliers at 68% even if Nembhard suits up. However, there's potential for the edge to grow considerably if he's ruled out, so I'd rather secure the 68% now and leave the door open for additional value. 
 Wizards vs Bulls: Wizards
 Trade 45% at Polymarket  → 
 I have serious concerns about the Chicago Bulls' ability to control the glass and protect the paint. The Bulls could also have to use lineup combinations they don't typically deploy together.
 Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis give the Washington Wizards a frontcourt pairing that can put heavy pressure on Chicago, especially with Trae Young running two-man actions with either big. The Bulls' frontcourt is anchored by Jalen Smith.
 The Bulls have been playing better basketball and picking up some wins lately, but 56% is simply too expensive for me to back them. I'll gladly take the Wizards at 45%.
 For more on this matchup, see our Wizards vs. Bulls prediction .
 Pelicans vs Thunder: Thunder
 Trade 83% at Polymarket  → 
 The Oklahoma City Thunder's mounting injuries have exposed some matchup vulnerabilities in recent games, but those shouldn't matter against the New Orleans Pelicans .
 Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara give Oklahoma City two 7-footers to wall off the paint against Zion Williamson and disrupt the Pelicans' offense.
 An 83% price on the Thunder might feel steep, but I have them closer to 88%.
 Suns vs Jazz: Suns
 Trade 63% at Polymarket  → 
 The Phoenix Suns have several perimeter players capable of creating their own offense in isolation, including Devin Booker , Jalen Green, and Miles Bridges.
 That's a major problem for a Utah Jazz defense missing its primary rim protectors. Utah is especially vulnerable to teams that hunt mismatches on the wings and at the point of attack.
 Phoenix should consistently target those weaknesses and generate efficient offense. The Jazz could also lack defensive energy in their third game in four nights.
 At 63%, give me the Suns on the moneyline.
 Kings vs Lakers: Lakers
 Trade 88% at Polymarket  → 
 Austin Reaves has been ruled out for the Los Angeles Lakers , and the market price on L.A. has climbed from 86% to 88%. 
 With Reaves sidelined, I project the Lakers to win 86% of the time against the Sacramento Kings . That makes 88% a price I'm not willing to buy. If you're looking to back the Lakers, I'd want to see the market dip below 86% before hitting the button. 
 That said, I'm not necessarily looking to flip to the Kings either. I price Sacramento at 14%, compared to its current 13% market price. While that technically gives the Kings a slight edge, a 1% pricing gap isn't enough to get me interested. 
 If the market holds at 88% for the Lakers and 13% for the Kings, Sacramento is technically the better play, but I'd rather wait for a better price on L.A. or pass on the matchup altogether. 
 Rockets vs Nuggets: Nuggets
 Trade 54% at Polymarket → 
 If you're surprised to see the Denver Nuggets trading as 54% favorites against the Houston Rockets , you're not alone.
 The market is reacting to the questionable status of Alperen Sengun , who left Wednesday's game with an eye injury and did not return.
 It's not just Sengun's potential absence that's concerning for Houston. Clint Capela is also questionable, while Steven Adams isn't equipped to handle heavy minutes at center against Nikola Jokic .
 At 54%, the size of the edge on Denver ultimately comes down to Sengun's availability. Check the NBA injury report for the latest updates before tipoff, and read our Rockets vs. Nuggets prediction for more on this game.

 The Magic have an edge at their current price against the Nets, and they have extra motivation on NBA Cup Friday as one of the few teams sitting at 2-0 in group play.
 I also like the Thunder here. They're 1-1 in group play but own a +30 point differential, and a win over the Pelicans would extend it. That could matter in a tiebreaker if they don't win the group outright.
